question.text: A MASTER-FEEDER structure is used by the Sahyadri Stat-Arb Fund. Which statement BEST captures its mechanics?

answer.text: Offshore investors subscribe into a feeder fund in Mauritius/Singapore/GIFT-IFSC, which in turn invests into the domestic master AIF in India; management fees are charged at the master level and only a nominal fee at the feeder
Each investor gets a separate managed account which feeds into a pooled vehicle
All investors — onshore and offshore — must subscribe only through the feeder
The master fund invests in multiple feeder funds which hold the portfolio

explanation.text: The Logic: Master-feeder: offshore investors pool into a feeder (often Mauritius/Singapore/GIFT-IFSC), and the feeder invests into the master fund in India. Direct investors can also invest in the master. Management fee is generally charged at the master level, with only a nominal fee at the feeder. The Trap: Option B describes managed accounts (not feeder). Option C is overstated — direct investors can invest in the master. Option D inverts the flow (master into feeders is wrong). Note: The workbook (pp. 128-130) describes master-feeder mechanics, direct investors in the master, and the master-level fee with nominal feeder fee.
